lesson_evidence.heading: The defining equation
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt: For a real square matrix $A$, a non-zero vector $v$ is an eigenvector when multiplication by $A$ changes only its scale. The defining relation is $$Av=\lambda v.$$ The scalar $\lambda$ is the associated eigenvalue. The vector must be non-zero: the zero vector satisfies $A0=\lambda0$ for every scalar, so it cannot identify an eigenvalue.
